back: Water, liquid or solid, falling from the atmosphere: rain, drizzle, hail, sleet, snow.
The temperature at which air becomes saturated; further cooling causes condensation.
Cooling of rising air because it expands as pressure falls (no heat removed).
Evaporation → uplift → adiabatic cooling → dew point → condensation on nuclei → droplets grow → fall.
Ground heating → air rises → cumulonimbus → heavy afternoon storms. Most of Zimbabwe's summer rain.
Moist air forced over high ground: rain on the windward side, rain shadow on the leeward side (sinking air warms and dries).
Warm air forced to rise over cold air at a front. Warm front: steady rain. Cold front: short, heavy showers.
Cool-season mist and drizzle on the Eastern Highlands, brought by moist south-east trade winds.
Form on surfaces on clear, calm nights. Frost when the dew point is below 0 °C.
